verses.1:1: Now it happened after Saul's death, once David had returned from striking down the Amalekites, that David stayed in Ziklag two days.
verses.1:2: On the third day, look, a man was coming from the camp, from Saul, with his garments torn and earth on his head. When he came to David, he fell to the ground and bowed down.
verses.1:3: David said to him, "Where are you coming from?" He answered him, "I escaped from Israel's camp."
verses.1:4: David said to him, "What took place? Please tell me." And he said, "The people fled from the battle, and many from the people also fell and died; Saul and his son Jonathan are dead as well."
verses.1:5: David said to the young man reporting to him, "How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan have died?"
verses.1:6: The young man reporting to him said, "I happened by chance to be on Mount Gilboa, and there was Saul leaning on his spear, and look, the chariots and horsemen were overtaking him.
verses.1:7: He turned around, saw me, and called to me, and I answered, 'Here I am.'
verses.1:8: He asked me, 'Who are you?' and I told him, 'I am an Amalekite.'
verses.1:9: Then he said to me, 'Please stand over me and put me to death, for agony has gripped me, because my life is still wholly in me.'
verses.1:10: So I stood over him and put him to death, because I knew that he would not live after his fall. Then I took the crown that was on his head and the armlet that was on his arm, and brought them here to my lord."
verses.1:11: Then David grasped his garments and tore them, as did all the men who were with him.
verses.1:12: They lamented and wept and fasted until evening over Saul and over his son Jonathan, and over the people of the LORD and over the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
verses.1:13: David asked the young man reporting to him, "Where are you from?" He replied, "I am the son of a resident alien, an Amalekite."
verses.1:14: David asked him, "How were you not afraid to reach out your hand to destroy the LORD's anointed?"
verses.1:15: Then David called one of the young men and said, "Step forward and strike him." So he struck him, and he died.
verses.1:16: And David said to him, "Your blood is on your own head, because your mouth has testified against you, saying, 'I myself put the LORD's anointed to death.'"
verses.1:17: Then David chanted this dirge over Saul and over his son Jonathan,
verses.1:18: and he directed that the sons of Judah be taught the Bow; see, it is written in the Book of Jashar:
verses.1:19: "Your splendor, Israel, lies pierced on your heights! How the warriors have fallen!
verses.1:20: Do not report it in Gath, do not announce it in the streets of Ashkelon, so that the daughters of the Philistines will not rejoice, so that the daughters of the uncircumcised will not triumph.
verses.1:21: Mountains in Gilboa, let no dew and no rain be on you, nor fields of offerings, for there the shield of warriors was polluted, the shield of Saul, unanointed with oil.
verses.1:22: From the blood of the pierced, from the fat of warriors, Jonathan's bow did not draw back, and Saul's sword would not return empty.
verses.1:23: Saul and Jonathan, loved and delightful in their lives, and in their death they were not separated; swifter than eagles were they, mightier than lions.
verses.1:24: Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who dressed you in scarlet with luxuries, who placed gold ornaments on your clothing.
verses.1:25: How the warriors have fallen in the middle of the battle! Jonathan lies pierced on your heights.
verses.1:26: I am in distress over you, my brother Jonathan; you were very delightful to me. More marvelous to me was your love than the love of women.
verses.1:27: How the warriors have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished!"
verses.2:1: Now after this, David inquired of the LORD, saying, "Should I go up into one of the cities of Judah?" The LORD answered him, "Go up." David asked, "Where should I go up?" And He replied, "To Hebron."
verses.2:2: So David went up there, and his two wives as well: Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail, the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
verses.2:3: And David brought up his men who were with him, each man and his household, and they settled in the cities of Hebron.
verses.2:4: Then the men of Judah came and anointed David there as king over the house of Judah. And they reported to David, saying, "The men of Jabesh-gilead are the ones who buried Saul."
verses.2:5: So David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead and told them, "Blessed are you by the LORD, because you have shown this loyal kindness to your lord, to Saul, and buried him.
verses.2:6: And now, may the LORD show you loyal kindness and faithfulness, and I myself will also do this good for you, because you have done this thing.
verses.2:7: So now let your hands grow strong, and be men of valor; for your lord Saul is dead, and the house of Judah has also anointed me as king over them."
verses.2:8: Meanwhile, Abner son of Ner, commander of Saul's army, had taken Ish-bosheth son of Saul and brought him across to Mahanaim.
verses.2:9: He made him king over Gilead, over the Ashurites, over Jezreel, over Ephraim, over Benjamin, and over all of Israel.
verses.2:10: Ish-bosheth son of Saul was forty years old when he began reigning over Israel, and he reigned for two years. However, the house of Judah followed David.
verses.2:11: The number of days that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.
verses.2:12: Now Abner son of Ner and the servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul marched out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
verses.2:13: Joab son of Zeruiah and the servants of David marched out and met them together by the pool of Gibeon. They sat down, these on one side of the pool and those on the other side of the pool.
verses.2:14: Abner said to Joab, "Please let the young men get up and compete in front of us." Joab answered, "Let them get up."
verses.2:15: So they got up and crossed over by number: twelve for Benjamin and for Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve from David's servants.
verses.2:16: Each man grasped his opponent by the head and drove his sword into his opponent's side, and they fell together. So that place was called Helkath-hazzurim, which is in Gibeon.
verses.2:17: The battle was exceedingly severe on that day, and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated before David's servants.
verses.2:18: Now the three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel was as swift on his feet as one of the gazelles in the field.
verses.2:19: Asahel pursued Abner, and he did not turn aside to go to the right or to the left from following Abner.
verses.2:20: Then Abner turned around and asked, "Is that you, Asahel?" He replied, "It is I."
verses.2:21: Abner told him, "Turn aside to your right or to your left, seize one of the young men for yourself, and take his armor for yourself." But Asahel was unwilling to turn away from following him.
verses.2:22: Once again Abner said to Asahel, "Turn away from following me! Why must I strike you to the ground? And how could I raise my face to Joab your brother?"
verses.2:23: Yet he refused to turn away, so Abner struck him in the abdomen with the back end of the spear, and the spear came out behind him. He fell there and died on the spot. And everyone who came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died stood still.
verses.2:24: However, Joab and Abishai pursued Abner. When the sun went down, they came as far as the hill of Ammah, which faces Giah on the road to the wilderness of Gibeon.
verses.2:25: The sons of Benjamin gathered themselves behind Abner and formed one troop, and they stood on the top of a hill.
verses.2:26: Abner called to Joab and said, "Is the sword to devour forever? Do you not know that it will end in bitterness? How long until you tell the people to turn back from following their brothers?"
verses.2:27: Joab replied, "As God lives, if you had not spoken, then surely in the morning the people would have withdrawn, each man from following his brother."
verses.2:28: So Joab blew the ram's horn, and all the people stood still; they did not pursue Israel anymore, nor did they fight again.
verses.2:29: Abner and his men marched through the Arabah all that night; they crossed the Jordan, marched through the whole of the Bithron, and came to Mahanaim.
verses.2:30: Now Joab turned back from following Abner and gathered all the people together, and from David's servants nineteen men and Asahel were missing.
verses.2:31: Yet the servants of David had struck down some from Benjamin and from Abner's men, so that three hundred and sixty men died.
verses.2:32: They carried Asahel and buried him in his father's tomb, which was in Bethlehem. Then Joab and his men marched all night, and daylight broke for them at Hebron.
verses.3:1: And the war was long between the house of Saul and the house of David; David kept growing stronger, and the house of Saul kept growing weaker.
verses.3:2: Sons were born to David in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelite.
verses.3:3: And his second was Chileab, by Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third was Absalom, the son of Maacah, the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur.
verses.3:4: And the fourth was Adonijah, the son of Haggith; and the fifth was Shephatiah, the son of Abital.
verses.3:5: And the sixth was Ithream, by Eglah, the wife of David. These were born to David in Hebron.
verses.3:6: Now while the war went on between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner was strengthening himself in the house of Saul.
verses.3:7: Now Saul had a concubine, and her name was Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah. And he said to Abner, "Why did you go in to my father's concubine?"
verses.3:8: And Abner became exceedingly angry at the words of Ish-bosheth, and he said, "Am I a dog's head belonging to Judah? Today I keep showing loyal kindness to the house of Saul your father, to his brothers and to his companions, and I have not handed you over into the hand of David; yet you call me to account for guilt regarding the woman today!
verses.3:9: May God do so to Abner, and add even more to him: just as the LORD swore to David, surely so I will do for him,
verses.3:10: to pass the kingdom over from the house of Saul and to raise up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan as far as Beersheba."
verses.3:11: And he was no longer able to return a word to Abner, because of his fear of him.
verses.3:12: Then Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, "Whose is the land?" and saying, "Make your covenant with me, and look, my hand is with you to turn all Israel around to you."
verses.3:13: And he said, "Good, I myself will make a covenant with you; only one thing I am asking from you, namely: you will not see my face unless you bring Michal the daughter of Saul first, when you come to see my face."
verses.3:14: Then David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, saying, "Give me my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines."
verses.3:15: And Ish-bosheth sent and took her away from her husband, from Paltiel the son of Laish.
verses.3:16: And her husband went with her, walking and weeping behind her as far as Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, "Go, turn back." And he turned back.
verses.3:17: Now Abner had a word with the elders of Israel, saying, "Already in days past you were seeking David to be king over you.
verses.3:18: Now then, do it! For the LORD has spoken concerning David, saying, 'By the hand of My servant David I will deliver My people Israel from the hand of the Philistines and from the hand of all their enemies.'"
verses.3:19: Abner also spoke in the ears of Benjamin; and Abner went as well to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that was good in the eyes of Israel and in the eyes of all the house of Benjamin.
verses.3:20: So Abner came to David at Hebron, and twenty men were with him. And David made a banquet for Abner and for the men who were with him.
verses.3:21: And Abner said to David, "Let me rise and go and gather all Israel to my lord the king, so that they may make a covenant with you, and you will reign over everything that your soul desires." Then David sent Abner off, and he went in peace.
verses.3:22: Now look, David's servants and Joab arrived from the raid, and they brought abundant plunder with them; and Abner was not with David in Hebron, because he had sent him off, and he had gone in peace.
verses.3:23: Now Joab and all the army that was with him came, and they reported to Joab, saying, "Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he sent him off, and he went in peace."
verses.3:24: Then Joab came to the king and said, "What have you done? Look, Abner came to you! Why then did you send him off, so that he is completely gone?
verses.3:25: You know Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive you, and to know your going out and your coming in, and to know everything that you are doing."
verses.3:26: Then Joab went out from David, and sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the cistern of Sirah; yet David did not know.
verses.3:27: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab turned him aside into the middle of the gate to speak with him privately; and he struck him there in the belly, and he died, for the blood of his brother Asahel.
verses.3:28: And David heard afterward and said, "I and my kingdom are guiltless before the LORD forever concerning the bloodshed of Abner the son of Ner.
verses.3:29: May it fall on Joab's head and on all his father's house; and may there never be cut off from the house of Joab anyone who has a discharge, or is afflicted with leprosy, or grasps a spindle, or falls by the sword, or lacks bread."
verses.3:30: Thus Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner, because he had put Asahel their brother to death at Gibeon in the battle.
verses.3:31: And David said to Joab and to all the people who were with him, "Tear your garments, wrap yourselves in sackcloth, and mourn in front of Abner." And King David was walking behind the bier.
verses.3:32: And they buried Abner in Hebron; the king raised his voice and wept by Abner's grave, and all the people wept.
verses.3:33: Then the king lamented over Abner and said, "Should Abner die the death of a fool?
verses.3:34: Your hands were not bound, and your feet were not placed in bronze shackles; as one falls before sons of injustice, you fell." And all the people wept over him once more.
verses.3:35: Then all the people came to give David bread to eat while it was still day; but David swore, saying, "May God do so to me, and add even more, if I taste bread or anything at all before the sun sets."
verses.3:36: And all the people observed this, and it was good in their eyes, just as everything the king did was good in the eyes of all the people.
verses.3:37: So all the people and all Israel knew on that day that it had not come from the king to put Abner the son of Ner to death.
verses.3:38: Then the king said to his servants, "Do you not know that a commander and a great man has fallen this day in Israel?
verses.3:39: And today I am weak, even though anointed king, while these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too harsh for me. May the LORD repay the one who does evil according to his evil."
verses.4:1: When the son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, his hands went limp, and all Israel was alarmed.
verses.4:2: Now two men, commanders of raiding bands, belonged to the son of Saul; the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the second was Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, from the sons of Benjamin, for Beeroth also is reckoned to Benjamin.
verses.4:3: And the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and they have been sojourning there until this day.
verses.4:4: Now Jonathan the son of Saul had a son whose feet were crippled. He was five years old when the report concerning Saul and Jonathan arrived from Jezreel; his nurse lifted him up and fled, and while she was hurrying to flee, he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.
verses.4:5: Then the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went and arrived about the heat of the day at the house of Ish-bosheth, while he was lying down for his midday rest.
verses.4:6: And in there they came as far as the middle of the house, fetching wheat, and they struck him in the belly; and Rechab and his brother Baanah escaped.
verses.4:7: Now they came into the house while he was lying on his bed in his bedroom, and they struck him and put him to death and removed his head; and they took his head and went along the way of the Arabah all night.
verses.4:8: And they brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David in Hebron and said to the king, "Here is the head of Ish-bosheth, the son of Saul, your enemy, who sought your life! And the LORD has granted my lord the king vengeance this day on Saul and on his offspring."
verses.4:9: Then David answered Rechab and his brother Baanah, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, "As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life from every distress,
verses.4:10: when someone reported to me, saying, 'Look, Saul is dead,' and in his own eyes he was like a bearer of good news, I seized him and killed him in Ziklag, which was the reward for good news that I gave him.
verses.4:11: How much more, when wicked men have killed a righteous man in his house, on his bed! Now then, shall I not demand his blood from your hand and purge you from the earth?"
verses.4:12: So David commanded the young men, and they killed them, severed their hands and their feet, and hung them up by the pool in Hebron. As for the head of Ish-bosheth, they took it and buried it in Abner's grave in Hebron.
verses.5:1: And all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and spoke, saying, "Here we are; we are your bone and your flesh.
verses.5:2: Even in times gone by, while Saul was king over us, you were the one bringing out and bringing in Israel. And the LORD said to you, 'You shall shepherd My people Israel, and you shall be leader over Israel.'"
verses.5:3: Then all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David cut a covenant with them in Hebron before the LORD, and they anointed David as king over Israel.
verses.5:4: David was thirty years of age when he began to reign; he reigned for forty years.
verses.5:5: In Hebron he reigned over Judah for seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned for thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.
verses.5:6: Then the king and his men marched to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, who lived in the land, and they told David, "You will not come in here; rather, the blind and the lame will turn you back," thinking, "David will not come in here."
verses.5:7: Yet David captured the fortress of Zion, which is the City of David.
verses.5:8: On that day David said, "Whoever strikes the Jebusites, let him reach the water shaft—and the lame and the blind, who are hated by David's soul!" For this reason people say, "Neither the blind nor the lame shall enter the house."
verses.5:9: David took up residence in the fortress and named it the City of David, and David built all around, from the Millo inward.
verses.5:10: And David went on growing greater, for the LORD, God of hosts, was with him.
verses.5:11: Then Hiram, king of Tyre, sent messengers to David, together with cedar timber, woodworkers, and stonemasons; and they built a house for David.
verses.5:12: Then David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and that He had lifted up his kingdom on account of His people Israel.
verses.5:13: David also took additional concubines and wives from Jerusalem after he had come from Hebron, and additional sons and daughters were born to David.
verses.5:14: These are the names of the ones born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
verses.5:17: Now the Philistines heard that they had anointed David as king over Israel, and all the Philistines went up to search for David. David heard and went down to the fortress.
verses.5:18: Now the Philistines had arrived and fanned out in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.5:19: So David inquired of the LORD, asking, "Should I go up against the Philistines? Will You deliver them into my hand?" And the LORD told David, "Go up, for I will indeed deliver the Philistines into your hand."
verses.5:20: Then David came to Baal-perazim, and David struck them down there; and he said, "The LORD has burst through my enemies before me like a burst of water." For this reason he called the name of that place Baal-perazim.
verses.5:21: And they left their idols behind there, and David and his men carried them off.
verses.5:22: Then the Philistines went up once more and fanned out in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.5:23: And David inquired of the LORD, and He said, "Do not go up; circle around to their rear and come upon them from opposite the balsam trees.
verses.5:24: And as soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then move decisively, for then the LORD has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines."
verses.5:25: David did so, just as the LORD commanded him, and he struck down the Philistines from Geba as far as the approach to Gezer.
verses.6:1: Then David once more gathered all the select men in Israel, thirty thousand.
verses.6:2: And David rose and went, together with all the people who were with him, from Baale-judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, over which is called the name, the name of the LORD of hosts who sits enthroned above the cherubim.
verses.6:3: They loaded the ark of God onto a new cart and carried it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill; and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, were driving the new cart.
verses.6:4: And they carried it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill, with the ark of God, while Ahio was walking in front of the ark.
verses.6:5: Now David and the entire house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD with all sorts of cypress-wood instruments, and with lyres, harps, tambourines, sistrums, and cymbals.
verses.6:6: When they arrived at the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached out to the ark of God and grasped it, for the oxen had stumbled.
verses.6:7: Then the anger of the LORD flared against Uzzah, and God struck him down there on account of the irreverence, and he died there beside the ark of God.
verses.6:8: And David became angry because the LORD had burst out with an outburst against Uzzah, and that place has been called Perez-uzzah to this day.
verses.6:9: And David feared the LORD on that day, and he said, "How will the ark of the LORD come to me?"
verses.6:10: So David was not willing to transfer the ark of the LORD to himself into the City of David; instead, David turned it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
verses.6:11: Now the ark of the LORD stayed in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and his entire household.
verses.6:12: Then it was reported to King David, saying, "The LORD has blessed the household of Obed-edom and all that is his on account of the ark of God." So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom into the City of David with joy.
verses.6:13: Now when those carrying the ark of the LORD had stepped six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf.
verses.6:14: And David was whirling with full strength before the LORD, and David was girded with a linen ephod.
verses.6:15: And David and the entire house of Israel were bringing up the ark of the LORD with shouting and with the sound of the ram's horn.
verses.6:16: Now as the ark of the LORD was entering the City of David, Michal, daughter of Saul, looked down through the window and saw King David leaping and whirling before the LORD, and she scorned him in her heart.
verses.6:17: Then they brought the ark of the LORD in and set it in its place in the midst of the tent that David had pitched for it; and David offered up burnt offerings before the LORD, as well as peace offerings.
verses.6:18: And David finished offering up the burnt offering and the peace offerings, and he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.
verses.6:19: Then he distributed to all the people, to the entire multitude of Israel, men and women alike, to each person one loaf of bread, one date cake, and one raisin cake. Then all the people departed, each to his house.
verses.6:20: When David came back to bless his household, Michal, daughter of Saul, went out to meet David and said, "How honored the king of Israel has made himself today, who uncovered himself today in the sight of the maidservants of his servants, just as one of the worthless fellows brazenly uncovers himself!"
verses.6:21: David replied to Michal, "It was before the LORD, who chose me over your father and over his entire house, to commission me as leader over the people of the LORD, over Israel; so I will celebrate before the LORD.
verses.6:22: And I will become even more lightly regarded than this, and I will be lowly in my own eyes; yet with the maidservants you spoke of, with them I will be honored."
verses.6:23: And as for Michal, daughter of Saul, she had no child until the day of her death.
verses.7:1: Now it happened, once the king had settled in his house and the LORD had given him rest all around from all his enemies,
verses.7:2: that the king said to Nathan the prophet, "Look now, I am dwelling in a house of cedars, while the ark of God is dwelling inside the tent curtain."
verses.7:3: And Nathan said to the king, "All that is in your heart, go and do, because the LORD is with you."
verses.7:4: Yet it happened during that same night that the word of the LORD came to Nathan, saying,
verses.7:5: "Go and say to My servant David, 'This is what the LORD says: Will you yourself build a house for Me to dwell in?
verses.7:6: For I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought the sons of Israel up out of Egypt down to this day; instead, I have been walking about in a tent and in a tabernacle.
verses.7:7: In every place where I walked about among all the sons of Israel, did I speak a word with any of the tribes of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd My people Israel, saying, "Why have you not built Me a house of cedars?"'
verses.7:8: Now then, say this to My servant David: 'This is what the LORD of hosts says: It was I who took you from the pasture, from behind the flock, to become leader over My people Israel.
verses.7:9: And I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you; and I will make for you a great name, like the name of the great ones who are on the earth.
verses.7:10: I will set a place for My people Israel and plant them, so that they may dwell in their own place and be unsettled no longer; and sons of injustice will not afflict them again as at the first,
verses.7:11: even from the day when I appointed judges over My people Israel; and I will give you rest from all your enemies. Moreover, the LORD announces to you that the LORD will make a house for you.
verses.7:12: When your days are full and you lie down with your fathers, I will raise up your seed after you, who will come out from your own body, and I will establish his kingdom.
verses.7:13: He is the one who will build a house for My name, and I will firmly establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
verses.7:14: I Myself will be a father to him, and he will be a son to Me. When he commits wrongdoing, I will reprove him with the rod of men and with the blows of the sons of mankind,
verses.7:15: yet My loyal kindness will not depart from him, as I removed it from Saul, whom I removed from before you.
verses.7:16: Your house and your kingdom will stand sure forever before you; your throne will remain established forever.'"
verses.7:17: In accordance with all these words and with this entire vision, so Nathan spoke to David.
verses.7:18: Then King David went in and sat before the LORD, and he said, "Who am I, Lord GOD, and what is my house, that You have brought me as far as this?
verses.7:19: Yet even this was small in Your eyes, Lord GOD, and You have spoken also about the house of Your servant for a distant future. And this is the instruction of mankind, Lord GOD!
verses.7:20: And what more can David still speak to You? For You know Your servant, Lord GOD.
verses.7:21: On account of Your word and in keeping with Your own heart, You have done all this greatness, to make it known to Your servant.
verses.7:22: Therefore You are great, LORD God, because there is no one like You, and there is no God apart from You, according to all that we have heard with our own ears.
verses.7:23: And who is like Your people, like Israel—one nation on the earth whom God went to redeem for Himself as a people, and to set a name for Himself, and to perform for you greatness and awesome deeds for Your land before Your people, whom You redeemed for Yourself from Egypt, from nations and their gods?
verses.7:24: And You firmly established for Yourself Your people Israel to be a people for Yourself forever, and You, LORD, became their God.
verses.7:25: And now, LORD God, uphold forever the word that You spoke about Your servant and about his house, and do just as You have spoken;
verses.7:26: and may Your name grow great forever, as it is said, 'The LORD of hosts is God over Israel,' and the house of Your servant David will remain established before You.
verses.7:27: For You, LORD of hosts, God of Israel, have uncovered the ear of Your servant, saying, 'I will build a house for you'; therefore Your servant has found his heart to pray this prayer to You.
verses.7:28: And now, Lord GOD, You Yourself are God, and Your words are truth, and You have spoken this good thing to Your servant.
verses.7:29: Now then, be pleased and bless the house of Your servant, so that it may endure forever before You; for You, Lord GOD, have spoken, and from Your blessing the house of Your servant will be blessed forever."
verses.8:1: Now it happened after this that David struck down the Philistines and subdued them, and David took Metheg-ammah out of the hand of the Philistines.
verses.8:2: He also struck down Moab and measured them with a cord, making them lie down on the ground; he measured off two cords to put to death and one full cord to keep alive. So Moab became servants to David, bearing tribute.
verses.8:3: David also struck down Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to restore his control at the Euphrates River.
verses.8:4: And David captured from him one thousand seven hundred horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers; David hamstrung all the chariot horses, yet spared from them enough for one hundred chariots.
verses.8:5: When Aram of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand men of Aram.
verses.8:6: Then David placed garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and Aram became servants to David, bearing tribute. And the LORD granted victory to David wherever he went.
verses.8:7: David also took the gold shields that were on the servants of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.
verses.8:8: And from Betah and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took a very large amount of bronze.
verses.8:9: Now Toi king of Hamath heard that David had struck down the entire army of Hadadezer,
verses.8:10: so Toi sent his son Joram to King David to inquire of his welfare and to bless him because he had fought against Hadadezer and struck him down, for Hadadezer had been at war with Toi. And in his hand were vessels of silver, vessels of gold, and vessels of bronze.
verses.8:11: King David consecrated these also to the LORD, along with the silver and the gold that he had consecrated from all the nations he had subjugated—
verses.8:12: from Aram, from Moab, from the sons of Ammon, from the Philistines, from Amalek, and from the plunder of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
verses.8:13: David also made a name for himself when he returned from striking down eighteen thousand of Aram in the Valley of Salt.
verses.8:14: He placed garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom he placed garrisons, and all Edom became servants to David. And the LORD granted victory to David wherever he went.
verses.8:15: So David reigned over all Israel, and David continually practiced justice and righteousness for all his people.
verses.8:16: Now Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;
verses.8:17: Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests, and Seraiah was scribe;
verses.8:18: and Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over both the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and the sons of David were priests.
verses.9:1: Then David said, "Is there still anyone left from the house of Saul, so that I may show loyal kindness to him for the sake of Jonathan?"
verses.9:2: Now the house of Saul had a servant whose name was Ziba, and they summoned him to David. The king said to him, "Are you Ziba?" And he said, "Your servant."
verses.9:3: The king said, "Is there not still someone of the house of Saul, so that I may show the loyal kindness of God to him?" And Ziba said to the king, "There is still a son of Jonathan, who is crippled in his feet."
verses.9:4: So the king said to him, "Where is he?" And Ziba said to the king, "Look, he is in the house of Machir son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar."
verses.9:5: Then King David sent and brought him from the house of Machir son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.
verses.9:6: When Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, son of Saul, came to David, he fell on his face and bowed down. And David said, "Mephibosheth!" And he said, "Here is your servant."
verses.9:7: David said to him, "Do not be afraid, for I will surely show loyal kindness to you for the sake of Jonathan your father; I will restore to you all the land of Saul your father, and you yourself will eat bread at my table continually."
verses.9:8: And he bowed down and said, "What is your servant, that you have turned toward a dead dog like me?"
verses.9:9: Then the king called Ziba, Saul's attendant, and said to him, "Everything that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to the son of your master.
verses.9:10: You are to work the ground for him—you, your sons, and your servants—and bring in the yield, so that the son of your master may have bread to eat; yet Mephibosheth, the son of your master, will continually eat bread at my table." Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
verses.9:11: Then Ziba said to the king, "According to all that my lord the king commands his servant, so your servant will do; and Mephibosheth eats at my table like one of the king's sons."
verses.9:12: Now Mephibosheth had a young son whose name was Mica, and all the residents of Ziba's house were servants to Mephibosheth.
verses.9:13: So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he continually ate at the king's table; and he was lame in both of his feet.
verses.10:1: Afterward it came about that the king of the sons of Ammon died, and his son Hanun reigned in his place.
verses.10:2: David said, "I will show loyal kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, just as his father showed loyal kindness to me." So David sent by the hand of his servants to comfort him regarding his father, and David's servants arrived in the land of the sons of Ammon.
verses.10:3: Then the officials of the sons of Ammon said to their lord Hanun, "Is David honoring your father in your eyes because he has sent comforters to you? Has David not sent his servants to you in order to examine the city, to spy it out, and to overthrow it?"
verses.10:4: So Hanun seized David's servants, shaved off half of their beards, cut off their garments in half up to their buttocks, and sent them away.
verses.10:5: When they told David, he sent to meet them, for the men were deeply humiliated. And the king said, "Remain in Jericho until your beards grow out, and then return."
verses.10:6: And the sons of Ammon saw that they had made themselves odious to David, so the sons of Ammon sent and hired the Arameans of Beth-rehob and the Arameans of Zobah, twenty thousand foot soldiers, and the king of Maacah with a thousand men, and the men of Tob, twelve thousand men.
verses.10:7: When David heard, he sent Joab and the entire army, the mighty warriors.
verses.10:8: The sons of Ammon came out and formed battle lines at the entrance of the gate, while the Arameans of Zobah and Rehob, and the men of Tob and Maacah, were by themselves in the field.
verses.10:9: When Joab saw that the battle front was against him both in front and behind, he selected from all the chosen men of Israel and formed lines against the Arameans.
verses.10:10: The rest of the people he placed into the hand of his brother Abishai, and he formed lines against the sons of Ammon.
verses.10:11: He said, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you shall be a help to me; and if the sons of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will go to help you.
verses.10:12: Be strong, and let us show ourselves strong for our people and for the cities of our God; and may the LORD do what is good in His eyes."
verses.10:13: Then Joab and the people who were with him drew near for battle against the Arameans, and they fled from before him.
verses.10:14: When the sons of Ammon saw that the Arameans had fled, they fled from before Abishai and entered the city. Then Joab turned back from the sons of Ammon and came to Jerusalem.
verses.10:15: When the Arameans saw that they had been routed before Israel, they gathered together.
verses.10:16: Hadadezer sent and brought out the Arameans who were beyond the River, and they came to Helam, with Shobach, commander of Hadadezer's army, before them.
verses.10:17: When it was reported to David, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and came to Helam. And the Arameans formed lines to meet David and fought with him.
verses.10:18: And the Arameans fled from before Israel, and David killed of the Arameans seven hundred charioteers and forty thousand horsemen; and he struck down Shobach, the commander of their army, so that he died there.
verses.10:19: When all the kings, the servants of Hadadezer, saw that they had been routed before Israel, they made peace with Israel and served them. So the Arameans feared to help the sons of Ammon anymore.
verses.11:1: It came about at the turn of the year, at the time when kings go out, that David sent Joab and his servants with him, along with all Israel, and they devastated the sons of Ammon and besieged Rabbah. But David remained in Jerusalem.
verses.11:2: It happened at the time of evening that David got up from his bed and walked about on the roof of the king's house; from the roof he saw a woman bathing, and the woman was very lovely in appearance.
verses.11:3: David sent and made inquiry about the woman, and someone said, "Is this not Bathsheba, daughter of Eliam, wife of Uriah the Hittite?"
verses.11:4: Then David sent messengers and took her. She came to him, and he lay with her. Now she had been purifying herself from her uncleanness. Then she returned to her house.
verses.11:5: And the woman conceived; so she sent and informed David, and said, "I am pregnant."
verses.11:6: So David sent to Joab, "Send Uriah the Hittite to me." And Joab sent Uriah to David.
verses.11:7: When Uriah came to him, David inquired how Joab was faring, how the people were faring, and how the war was faring.
verses.11:8: Then David said to Uriah, "Go down to your house and wash your feet." So Uriah went out from the king's house, and a gift from the king went out after him.
verses.11:9: But Uriah lay down at the entrance of the king's house with all his lord's servants, and he did not go down to his house.
verses.11:10: And they reported to David, saying, "Uriah has not gone down to his house." So David said to Uriah, "Are you not coming from a journey? Why have you not gone down to your house?"
verses.11:11: Uriah said to David, "The ark and Israel and Judah are staying in booths, and my lord Joab and my lord's servants are encamped on the open field; should I then go to my house to eat and to drink and to lie with my wife? By your life and by the life of your soul, I will not do this thing."
verses.11:12: Then David said to Uriah, "Remain here today as well, and tomorrow I will send you away." So Uriah remained in Jerusalem that day and the following day.
verses.11:13: And David invited him, and he ate and drank in his presence, and David made him drunk. In the evening he went out to lie down on his bed with his lord's servants, but to his house he did not go down.
verses.11:14: It came about in the morning that David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by Uriah's hand.
verses.11:15: And he wrote in the letter, saying, "Place Uriah directly at the front of the fierce battle, and pull back from behind him, so that he will be struck down and die."
verses.11:16: And it came about, as Joab kept watch over the city, that he assigned Uriah to the place where he knew men of valor were.
verses.11:17: Then the men of the city came out and fought with Joab, and some of the people, from among David's servants, fell; Uriah the Hittite died as well.
verses.11:18: Then Joab sent and informed David of all the events of the battle.
verses.11:19: And he commanded the messenger, saying, "When you have finished telling all the events of the battle to the king,
verses.11:20: then if the king's fury rises and he says to you, 'Why did you draw near to the city to fight? Did you not know that they would shoot from atop the wall?
verses.11:21: Who struck down Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth? Did not a woman throw an upper millstone on him from atop the wall so that he died at Thebez? Why did you draw near to the wall?' then you shall say, 'Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well.'"
verses.11:22: So the messenger went, arrived, and reported to David everything for which Joab had sent him.
verses.11:23: The messenger said to David, "The men overpowered us and came out against us into the field, yet we pressed upon them as far as the entrance of the gate.
verses.11:24: Then the archers shot at your servants from atop the wall, and some of the king's servants died; and your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well."
verses.11:25: Then David said to the messenger, "This is what you shall say to Joab, 'Do not let this thing be evil in your eyes, for the sword devours this one as well as that; strengthen your battle against the city and tear it down.' And encourage him."
verses.11:26: When Uriah's wife heard that her husband Uriah had died, she lamented over her husband.
verses.11:27: When the mourning had passed, David sent and brought her into his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. Yet the thing that David had done was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.12:1: Then the LORD sent Nathan to David. He came to him and said to him, "Two men were in the same city, one wealthy and one poor.
verses.12:2: The wealthy man had flocks and herds in great abundance.
verses.12:3: But the poor man had nothing at all except one small ewe lamb that he had bought. He nourished her, and she grew up together with him and his children; she would eat from his own piece of bread, drink from his cup, and lie in his arms, and she was like a daughter to him.
verses.12:4: Now a traveler came to the wealthy man, and he begrudged taking from his own flock or his own herd to prepare for the wayfarer who had come to him; instead, he took the poor man's ewe lamb and prepared her for the man who had come to him."
verses.12:5: Then David's anger flared fiercely against the man, and he said to Nathan, "As the LORD lives, the man who did this is worthy of death!
verses.12:6: And he must repay the ewe lamb fourfold, because he did this thing and because he had no compassion."
verses.12:7: Then Nathan said to David, "You are the man! This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I Myself anointed you as king over Israel, and I Myself rescued you from the hand of Saul.
verses.12:8: I gave you your master's house and your master's wives into your arms, and I gave you the house of Israel and Judah; and if that were too little, I would have added for you as much again and more.
verses.12:9: Why have you despised the word of the LORD, by doing what is evil in My eyes? You struck down Uriah the Hittite with the sword, you took his wife for yourself as a wife, and you killed him by the sword of the sons of Ammon.
verses.12:10: And now, the sword will not depart from your house forever, because you despised Me and took the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be a wife for yourself.'
verses.12:11: This is what the LORD says: 'Look, I am raising up calamity against you out of your own house; and I will take your wives before your very eyes and give them to your neighbor, and he will lie with your wives before the eyes of this sun.
verses.12:12: For you acted in secret, but I Myself will do this thing in front of all Israel and in front of the sun.'"
verses.12:13: Then David said to Nathan, "I have sinned against the LORD." And Nathan replied to David, "The LORD also has removed your sin; you will not die.
verses.12:14: However, because by this deed you have caused the enemies of the LORD to show utter contempt, the son who has been born to you will also surely die."
verses.12:15: Then Nathan went to his house. And the LORD struck the child that Uriah's wife had borne to David, and he fell gravely ill.
verses.12:16: So David sought God on behalf of the boy; David kept a fast, and he would go inside and spend the night, lying upon the ground.
verses.12:17: The elders of his house stood over him to lift him up from the ground, but he was unwilling, and he would not eat food with them.
verses.12:18: Then on the seventh day it happened that the child died. David's servants were afraid to tell him that the child had died, for they said, "Look, while the child was alive, we spoke to him and he did not listen to our voice. How then can we say to him, 'The child is dead'? He may do harm!"
verses.12:19: And David saw that his servants were whispering to one another, and David understood that the child was dead. Then David said to his servants, "Is the child dead?" And they replied, "He is dead."
verses.12:20: Then David got up from the ground, washed, anointed himself, and changed his garments; and he went into the house of the LORD and worshiped. Then he came to his own house, and when he asked, they set food before him, and he ate.
verses.12:21: Then his servants said to him, "What is this thing that you have done? On account of the child while he was alive, you fasted and wept, yet when the child died, you got up and ate food."
verses.12:22: He answered, "While the child was still alive, I fasted and wept; for I said, 'Who knows? The LORD may be gracious to me, and the child may live.'
verses.12:23: Now, however, he is dead; why then am I fasting? Am I able to bring him back again? I am going to him, but he will not come back to me."
verses.12:24: Then David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and went in to her and lay with her. She bore a son, and she called his name Solomon; and the LORD loved him.
verses.12:25: And He sent word by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and he called his name Jedidiah, for the sake of the LORD.
verses.12:26: Now Joab fought against Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, and he captured the royal city.
verses.12:27: Then Joab sent messengers to David and said, "I have fought against Rabbah, and I have also captured the city of waters.
verses.12:28: So now, gather the rest of the people, encamp against the city, and capture it; otherwise I myself will capture the city, and my name will be called over it."
verses.12:29: Then David gathered all the people and went to Rabbah; he fought against it and captured it.
verses.12:30: And he took the crown of their king from his head, and its weight was a talent of gold with a precious stone, and it was on David's head. He also brought out the spoil of the city in great abundance.
verses.12:31: And he brought out the people who were in it and set them to the saw, and to iron picks, and to iron axes, and made them pass through the brickkiln; and thus he did to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
verses.13:1: Now it happened after this that Absalom son of David had a beautiful sister whose name was Tamar, and Amnon son of David loved her.
verses.13:2: And Amnon was so tormented that he made himself ill on account of Tamar his sister, for she was a virgin, and it seemed impossible in Amnon's eyes to do anything to her.
verses.13:3: Now Amnon had a friend whose name was Jonadab, son of Shimeah, David's brother; and Jonadab was a very shrewd man.
verses.13:4: He said to him, "Why are you so gaunt, son of the king, morning after morning? Will you not tell me?" And Amnon said to him, "It is Tamar, the sister of my brother Absalom, whom I love."
verses.13:5: Then Jehonadab said to him, "Lie down on your bed and pretend to be ill. When your father comes to see you, say to him, 'Please let my sister Tamar come and give me food to eat, and prepare the meal before my eyes, so that I may watch and eat from her hand.'"
verses.13:6: So Amnon lay down and pretended to be ill. When the king came to see him, Amnon said to the king, "Please let my sister Tamar come and make two cakes in front of my eyes, so that I may eat from her hand."
verses.13:7: Then David sent word to Tamar at home, saying, "Please go to the house of your brother Amnon and prepare the meal for him."
verses.13:8: So Tamar went to the house of her brother Amnon, while he was lying down. She took the dough, kneaded it, shaped the cakes before his eyes, and cooked the cakes.
verses.13:9: Then she took the pan and poured them out before him, but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, "Send every man out from my presence." So every man went out from his presence.
verses.13:10: Then Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the meal into the inner room, that I may eat from your hand." So Tamar took the cakes she had made and brought them into the inner room to her brother Amnon.
verses.13:11: When she brought them close for him to eat, he seized hold of her and said to her, "Come, lie with me, my sister."
verses.13:12: But she said to him, "No, my brother, do not violate me! For such a thing is not done in Israel; do not commit this outrageous folly.
verses.13:13: As for me, where could I carry my disgrace? And as for you, you would be like one of the fools in Israel. Now please speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you."
verses.13:14: Yet he was unwilling to listen to her voice, and he overpowered her, violated her, and lay with her.
verses.13:15: Then Amnon hated her with an exceedingly great hatred, for greater was the hatred with which he hated her than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, "Rise up, go!"
verses.13:16: And she said to him, "No, because this great evil of sending me away is greater than the other that you did to me!" But he was unwilling to listen to her.
verses.13:17: Then he summoned his young man, his attendant, and said, "Send this one away from my presence outside, and bolt the door behind her."
verses.13:18: Now she was wearing a long-sleeved tunic, for such robes the virgin daughters of the king used to wear. And his attendant brought her outside and bolted the door behind her.
verses.13:19: Then Tamar put ashes on her head, and she tore the long-sleeved tunic that was on her; she placed her hand on her head and went away, crying aloud as she went.
verses.13:20: Then her brother Absalom said to her, "Has your brother Aminon been with you? Now, my sister, keep silent; he is your brother. Do not take this matter to heart." So Tamar remained, desolate, in the house of her brother Absalom.
verses.13:21: Now King David heard all these things, and he grew very angry.
verses.13:22: But Absalom did not speak with Amnon, either bad or good, for Absalom hated Amnon because he had violated his sister Tamar.
verses.13:23: Then after two full years it happened that Absalom had sheepshearers at Baal-hazor, which is near Ephraim, and Absalom invited all the king's sons.
verses.13:24: And Absalom came to the king and said, "Look now, your servant has sheepshearers; please let the king and his servants go with your servant."
verses.13:25: But the king said to Absalom, "No, my son, let us not all go, so that we do not become a burden to you." He pressed him, but he was unwilling to go, and he blessed him.
verses.13:26: Then Absalom said, "If not, then please let my brother Amnon go with us." And the king replied to him, "Why should he go with you?"
verses.13:27: But Absalom pressed him, so he sent Amnon and all the king's sons with him.
verses.13:28: Then Absalom commanded his young men, saying, "Watch now: when Amnon's heart is merry with wine and I say to you, 'Strike Amnon,' then put him to death. Do not be afraid; have I not myself commanded you? Be strong and be men of valor!"
verses.13:29: So Absalom's young men did to Amnon just as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king's sons rose up, each man mounted his mule, and they fled.
verses.13:30: Now while they were on the way, the report came to David, saying, "Absalom has struck down all the king's sons, and not one of them is left!"
verses.13:31: Then the king rose, tore his garments, and lay on the ground; and all his servants stood by with their garments torn.
verses.13:32: Then Jonadab, son of Shimeah, David's brother, answered and said, "Let not my lord say, 'They have put to death all the young men, the king's sons,' for Amnon alone is dead; for by Absalom's command this has been determined since the day he violated his sister Tamar.
verses.13:33: So now, let not my lord the king take such a thing to heart, saying, 'All the king's sons are dead,' for Amnon alone is dead."
verses.13:34: Now Absalom fled. And the young man keeping watch lifted up his eyes and saw: look, many people were coming from the road behind him, from the side of the mountain.
verses.13:35: Then Jonadab said to the king, "Look, the king's sons have come! According to the word of your servant, so it has happened."
verses.13:36: And just as he finished speaking, look, the king's sons came, and they lifted up their voice and wept; and the king and all his servants also wept with a very great weeping.
verses.13:37: Now Absalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And he mourned for his son day after day.
verses.13:38: So Absalom fled and went to Geshur, and he was there three years.
verses.13:39: And King David longed to go out to Absalom, for he was comforted concerning Amnon, since he was dead.
verses.14:1: Now Joab son of Zeruiah knew that the king's heart was toward Absalom.
verses.14:2: So Joab sent to Tekoa, took a wise woman from there, and told her, "Please act as a mourner, put on garments of mourning, and do not anoint yourself with oil; be like a woman who has been mourning over a dead person these many days.
verses.14:3: Go in to the king and speak to him in this way." Then Joab put the words into her mouth.
verses.14:4: The Tekoite woman spoke to the king; she fell on her face to the ground, bowed down, and said, "Help, King!"
verses.14:5: The king said to her, "What is the matter with you?" She answered, "Truly, I am a widow, for my husband has died.
verses.14:6: Your maidservant had two sons, and the two of them fought in the field with no one to intervene between them; the one struck the other and killed him.
verses.14:7: And now the entire clan has risen up against your maidservant, saying, 'Hand over the one who struck his brother, so that we may put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed, and destroy the heir as well!' So they will extinguish my ember that remains, leaving my husband neither name nor remnant on the face of the earth."
verses.14:8: The king said to the woman, "Go to your house, and I will give orders concerning you."
verses.14:9: The Tekoite woman said to the king, "My lord the king, let the guilt be on me and on my father's house, and may the king and his throne be guiltless."
verses.14:10: The king said, "Whoever speaks to you, bring him to me, and he will not touch you again."
verses.14:11: She said, "Please let the king remember the LORD your God, so that the avenger of blood may not increase the ruin, and so that they do not destroy my son." He answered, "As the LORD lives, not a single hair of your son will fall to the ground."
verses.14:12: Then the woman said, "Please let your maidservant speak a word to my lord the king." He said, "Speak."
verses.14:13: The woman said, "Why then have you devised such a thing against the people of God? In speaking this word, the king is like one who is guilty, because the king does not bring back his banished one.
verses.14:14: For we must surely die, and we are like water poured out on the ground that cannot be gathered up; yet God does not take away a life, but He devises plans so that a banished one will not remain banished from Him.
verses.14:15: Now the reason I have come to speak this matter to the king my lord is that the people made me afraid; so your maidservant said, 'Let me please speak to the king; perhaps the king will carry out the request of his maidservant.
verses.14:16: For the king will hear and rescue his maidservant from the hand of the man who would destroy both me and my son together from the inheritance of God.'
verses.14:17: And your maidservant said, 'Please let the word of my lord the king bring rest,' for my lord the king is like the angel of God in hearing good and evil. And may the LORD your God be with you."
verses.14:18: Then the king answered and said to the woman, "Please do not hide from me anything that I am asking you." And the woman said, "Please let my lord the king speak."
verses.14:19: The king said, "Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?" The woman answered and said, "As your soul lives, my lord the king, there is no turning to the right or to the left from anything that my lord the king has spoken. Indeed, it was your servant Joab who commanded me, and it was he who put all these words into the mouth of your maidservant.
verses.14:20: In order to change the face of the matter, your servant Joab has done this thing. Yet my lord is wise, like the wisdom of the angel of God, to know everything that is in the land."
verses.14:21: Then the king said to Joab, "Look now, I have done this thing; go and bring back the young man Absalom."
verses.14:22: Joab fell on his face to the ground, bowed down, and blessed the king. Then Joab said, "Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your eyes, my lord the king, because the king has carried out the request of your servant."
verses.14:23: So Joab arose, went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
verses.14:24: However, the king said, "Let him turn aside to his own house, and let him not see my face." So Absalom turned aside to his own house and did not see the face of the king.
verses.14:25: Now in all Israel there was no man as handsome as Absalom, so greatly praised; from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head, there was no blemish in him.
verses.14:26: When he shaved his head—for at the end of every year he would shave it because it became heavy on him, so he shaved it—he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels by the king's weight.
verses.14:27: To Absalom were born three sons and one daughter, whose name was Tamar; she was a woman beautiful in appearance.
verses.14:28: Absalom lived in Jerusalem two full years, yet he did not see the face of the king.
verses.14:29: Then Absalom sent for Joab to send him to the king, but he was unwilling to come to him. So he sent again a second time, and he was unwilling to come.
verses.14:30: Therefore he said to his servants, "Look, Joab's field is next to mine, and he has barley there; go and set it on fire." So Absalom's servants set the field on fire.
verses.14:31: Then Joab arose, came to Absalom at the house, and said to him, "Why have your servants set my field on fire?"
verses.14:32: Absalom said to Joab, "Look, I sent to you, saying, 'Come here so that I may send you to the king to say, "Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me if I were still there."' Now therefore, let me see the king's face; and if there is guilt in me, let him put me to death."
verses.14:33: So Joab went to the king and told him. Then the king summoned Absalom, and he came to the king and bowed down to him on his face to the ground before the king. And the king kissed Absalom.
verses.15:1: Now after this, Absalom provided for himself a chariot and horses, along with fifty men running before him.
verses.15:2: Absalom would rise early and stand beside the road to the gate. Whenever any man had a dispute to come to the king for judgment, Absalom would call to him and say, "From which city are you?" And he would reply, "Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel."
verses.15:3: Then Absalom would say to him, "See, your claims are good and right, yet there is no one from the king to hear you."
verses.15:4: Moreover, Absalom would say, "If only someone would make me judge in the land! Then every man who has a dispute or case would come to me, and I would give him justice."
verses.15:5: And whenever a man approached to bow down to him, he would stretch out his hand, take hold of him, and kiss him.
verses.15:6: In this way Absalom treated all of Israel who came to the king for judgment, and so Absalom stole the heart of the men of Israel.
verses.15:7: At the end of forty years, Absalom said to the king, "Please let me go and pay my vow, which I vowed to the LORD, in Hebron.
verses.15:8: For your servant vowed a vow while I lived at Geshur in Aram, saying, 'If the LORD indeed brings me back to Jerusalem, then I will serve the LORD.'"
verses.15:9: The king said to him, "Go in peace." So he arose and went to Hebron.
verses.15:10: Then Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, you shall say, 'Absalom has become king in Hebron!'"
verses.15:11: Now two hundred men from Jerusalem went with Absalom; they were invited guests who went in their innocence, and they did not know anything.
verses.15:12: While he was offering the sacrifices, Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor, from his city, from Giloh. And the conspiracy grew strong, for the people with Absalom kept increasing.
verses.15:13: Then a messenger came to David, saying, "The heart of the men of Israel has gone after Absalom."
verses.15:14: So David said to all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem, "Arise and let us flee, for there will be no escape for us from Absalom. Hurry to leave, or else he will hurry and overtake us, bring disaster down upon us, and strike the city with the edge of the sword."
verses.15:15: The king's servants said to the king, "According to everything my lord the king chooses, here are your servants."
verses.15:16: So the king went out with all his household following him; however, the king left ten concubines to keep the house.
verses.15:17: The king went out with all the people following him, and they stopped at the distant house.
verses.15:18: All his servants passed by beside him, and all the Cherethites, all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who had come after him from Gath, passed on before the king.
verses.15:19: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why should you also go with us? Return and stay with the king, for you are a foreigner and also an exile from your own place.
verses.15:20: Yesterday was your arrival, and today should I make you wander about with us while I am going wherever I am going? Return and take your brothers back with you; may loyal love and faithfulness be yours."
verses.15:21: Ittai answered the king and said, "As the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, indeed in the place where my lord the king is, whether for death or for life, surely there your servant will be."
verses.15:22: David said to Ittai, "Go and pass on." So Ittai the Gittite passed on, with all his men and all the little ones who were with him.
verses.15:23: The whole countryside was weeping with a loud voice while all the people passed by. The king crossed the Kidron Valley, and all the people passed on toward the road to the wilderness.
verses.15:24: Now Zadok too, and all the Levites with him, were carrying the ark of the covenant of God. They set down the ark of God, and Abiathar came up until all the people had finished passing out of the city.
verses.15:25: Then the king said to Zadok, "Return the ark of God to the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, He will bring me back and show me both it and His dwelling place.
verses.15:26: But if He says this, 'I take no delight in you,' here I am; let Him do to me what is good in His eyes."
verses.15:27: The king also said to Zadok the priest, "Are you a seer? Return to the city in peace, along with Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan son of Abiathar, your two sons with you.
verses.15:28: See, I will wait in the plains of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me."
verses.15:29: So Zadok and Abiathar returned the ark of God to Jerusalem, and they stayed there.
verses.15:30: Meanwhile David went up the ascent of the Olives, weeping as he went up, with his head covered, and walking barefoot. All the people who were with him each covered his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up.
verses.15:31: Now someone told David, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." And David said, "Please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness, LORD."
verses.15:32: When David arrived at the summit, where God was worshiped, there to meet him was Hushai the Archite, with his tunic torn and earth on his head.
verses.15:33: David said to him, "If you pass on with me, you will be a burden to me.
verses.15:34: But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, 'I will be your servant, King; just as I was your father's servant in time past, so now I will be your servant,' then you will frustrate the counsel of Ahithophel for me.
verses.15:35: Are not Zadok and Abiathar the priests there with you? Therefore, everything that you hear from the king's house, you shall report to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
verses.15:36: Look, their two sons are there with them—Ahimaaz, Zadok's son, and Jonathan, Abiathar's son—and by their hand you shall send to me everything that you hear."
verses.15:37: So Hushai, David's friend, came into the city, just as Absalom was entering Jerusalem.
verses.16:1: Now David had passed a short distance beyond the summit, and there was Ziba, Mephibosheth's servant, coming to meet him with a pair of saddled donkeys, and on them were two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred clusters of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a skin of wine.
verses.16:2: The king said to Ziba, "What do you have these for?" And Ziba replied, "The donkeys are for the king's household to ride on, the bread and the summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine is for the weary to drink in the wilderness."
verses.16:3: The king asked, "And where is your master's son?" Ziba said to the king, "Look, he is staying in Jerusalem, for he said, 'Today the house of Israel will restore my father's kingdom to me.'"
verses.16:4: Then the king said to Ziba, "Look, everything that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours." And Ziba said, "I bow down; may I find favor in your sight, my lord the king."
verses.16:5: When King David reached Bahurim, a man from the clan of the house of Saul came out from there; his name was Shimei son of Gera, and he came out cursing continuously.
verses.16:6: He threw stones at David and at all the servants of King David, while all the people and all the mighty men were on his right and on his left.
verses.16:7: This is what Shimei said as he cursed: "Get out! Get out, man of bloodshed and worthless man!
verses.16:8: The LORD has brought back upon you all the bloodshed of the house of Saul, in whose place you reigned, and the LORD has given the kingship into the hand of your son Absalom. Now look, you are in your own calamity, because you are a man of bloodshed!"
verses.16:9: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, "Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Please let me cross over and take off his head."
verses.16:10: The king replied, "What is there between me and you, sons of Zeruiah? So let him curse, because the LORD has told him, 'Curse David.' Who then can say, 'Why have you done this?'"
verses.16:11: David also said to Abishai and to all his servants, "Look, my own son, who came from my own body, is seeking my life! How much more now this Benjamite! Leave him alone and let him curse, for the LORD has told him to.
verses.16:12: Perhaps the LORD will look upon my eye, and the LORD will return good to me in place of his cursing this day."
verses.16:13: So David and his men continued on the road, while Shimei walked along the hillside opposite him, cursing as he went, throwing stones across at him, and flinging dust.
verses.16:14: The king and all the people who were with him arrived weary, and he refreshed himself there.
verses.16:15: Meanwhile, Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.
verses.16:16: Now when Hushai the Archite, David's friend, came to Absalom, Hushai said to Absalom, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"
verses.16:17: Absalom said to Hushai, "Is this your loyalty to your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?"
verses.16:18: Hushai answered Absalom, "No! Rather, the one whom the LORD and this people and all the men of Israel have chosen—his I will be, and with him I will stay.
verses.16:19: And secondly, whom should I serve? Should it not be before his son? Just as I served before your father, so I will be before you."
verses.16:20: Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Give your counsel: what should we do?"
verses.16:21: Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Go in to your father's concubines, whom he left behind to keep the house; then all Israel will hear that you have made yourself a stench to your father, and the hands of all who are with you will grow strong."
verses.16:22: So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and Absalom went in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.
verses.16:23: Now the counsel of Ahithophel that he gave in those days was as if someone inquired of the word of God; so was all the counsel of Ahithophel, both to David and to Absalom.
verses.17:1: Then Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Please let me choose twelve thousand men, and I will rise and pursue David tonight.
verses.17:2: I will come upon him while he is weary and his hands are weak, and I will throw him into panic; all the people who are with him will flee, and I will strike down the king alone.
verses.17:3: And I will bring all the people back to you. The man whom you seek means the return of everyone; all the people will be at peace."
verses.17:4: The proposal seemed right in the eyes of Absalom and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel.
verses.17:5: Then Absalom said, "Please summon Hushai the Archite as well, and let us hear what is in his mouth too."
verses.17:6: When Hushai came to Absalom, Absalom spoke to him, saying, "Ahithophel has spoken words like this. Should we carry out his word? If not, you speak."
verses.17:7: Hushai said to Absalom, "This time, the counsel that Ahithophel has given is not good."
verses.17:8: Hushai continued, "You yourself know your father and his men, that they are mighty men, and they are bitter of soul, like a bear robbed of her cubs in the field. Furthermore, your father is a man of war and will not spend the night with the people.
verses.17:9: Look, even now he is hidden in one of the pits or in some other place. And when some fall among them at the very start, whoever hears of it will say, 'There has been a slaughter among the people who follow Absalom.'
verses.17:10: Then even the valiant man whose heart is like the heart of a lion will utterly melt away, for all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man and that those who are with him are valiant men.
verses.17:11: Therefore I counsel that all Israel be completely gathered to you, from Dan even to Beersheba, like the sand by the sea in multitude, and that you go into battle in person.
verses.17:12: Then we will come upon him in one of the places where he is found, and we will settle upon him just as the dew falls on the ground; and of him and of all the men who are with him, not even one will be left.
verses.17:13: And if he withdraws into a city, then all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down to the valley until not even a pebble is found there."
verses.17:14: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel." For the LORD had ordained to thwart the good counsel of Ahithophel, so that the LORD might bring disaster upon Absalom.
verses.17:15: Then Hushai said to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, "In such and such a way Ahithophel counseled Absalom and the elders of Israel, and in such and such a way I myself counseled.
verses.17:16: Now then, send quickly and tell David, 'Do not spend this night on the plains of the wilderness, but by all means cross over, or else the king and all the people who are with him will be swallowed up.'"
verses.17:17: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En-rogel; a servant girl would go and tell them, and they would go and tell King David, because they could not be seen entering the city.
verses.17:18: However, a young man saw them and told Absalom. So both of them went quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim who had a well in his courtyard, and they went down into it.
verses.17:19: The woman took a covering and spread it over the mouth of the well, and scattered crushed grain on top of it, and nothing was known.
verses.17:20: When Absalom's servants came to the woman at the house, they asked, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" The woman said to them, "They have crossed the stream of water." They searched but did not find them, so they returned to Jerusalem.
verses.17:21: After they had gone, the two came up out of the well, went on, and reported to King David. They said to David, "Rise and cross the water quickly, for Ahithophel has counseled like this against you."
verses.17:22: Then David and all the people who were with him rose and crossed the Jordan. By the light of morning, not even one was missing who had not crossed the Jordan.
verses.17:23: Now when Ahithophel saw that his counsel had not been followed, he saddled his donkey, rose, and went to his house, to his own city. He put his household in order and hanged himself; so he died and was buried in the tomb of his father.
verses.17:24: Then David came to Mahanaim, while Absalom crossed the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.
verses.17:25: Absalom set Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Now Amasa was the son of a man whose name was Ithra the Israelite, who had gone in to Abigail daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, the mother of Joab.
verses.17:26: And Israel and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead.
verses.17:27: When David came to Mahanaim, Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim—
verses.17:28: bedding, basins, pottery vessels, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, roasted seeds,
verses.17:29: honey, curds, sheep, and cheese from the herd—brought them to David and to the people who were with him to eat, for they said, "The people are hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness."
verses.18:1: David mustered the people who were with him and placed over them captains of thousands and captains of hundreds.
verses.18:2: David sent out the people, a third under the hand of Joab, a third under the hand of Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and a third under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the people, "I too will certainly go out with you."
verses.18:3: But the people said, "You must not go out! For if we indeed flee, they will not set their mind on us; and if half of us die, they will not set their mind on us, for now there are ten thousand like us. So now it is better that you be there for us to help from the city."
verses.18:4: The king said to them, "Whatever is good in your eyes I will do." So the king stood at the side of the gate, while all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.
verses.18:5: The king commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, saying, "Be gentle for my sake with the young man Absalom." And all the people heard when the king commanded all the captains concerning Absalom.
verses.18:6: Then the people went out into the field to meet Israel, and the battle was in the forest of Ephraim.
verses.18:7: There the people of Israel were routed before the servants of David, and the slaughter there on that day was great, twenty thousand.
verses.18:8: And the battle there was spread out across the face of all the land, and the forest devoured more of the people than the sword devoured on that day.
verses.18:9: And Absalom happened to come before the servants of David. Absalom was riding on the mule, and the mule went under the tangled branches of the great terebinth, and his head caught fast in the terebinth; so he was left between heaven and earth, while the mule that was under him passed on.
verses.18:10: A certain man saw it and told Joab, saying, "Look, I saw Absalom hanging in the terebinth."
verses.18:11: Joab said to the man who had told him, "Look, you saw him! Why then did you not strike him there to the ground? It would have been my part to give you ten pieces of silver and a belt."
verses.18:12: The man said to Joab, "Even if I weighed a thousand pieces of silver in my palms, I would not stretch out my hand against the king's son; for the king commanded you, Abishai, and Ittai in our hearing, saying, 'Protect the young man Absalom, whoever you are.'
verses.18:13: Otherwise, had I acted deceitfully against my own life—and nothing is hidden from the king—you yourself would have stood at a distance."
verses.18:14: Joab said, "I will not linger like this before you." And he took three javelins in his hand and drove them into the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the heart of the terebinth.
verses.18:15: Ten young men who carried Joab's weapons circled around, struck Absalom, and put him to death.
verses.18:16: Joab sounded the ram's horn, and the people turned back from pursuing Israel, for Joab held the people back.
verses.18:17: They took Absalom and threw him into the great pit in the forest, and they raised up over him a very great heap of stones. And all Israel fled, every man to his tent.
verses.18:18: Now during his lifetime Absalom had taken and raised up for himself the pillar that is in the King's Valley, for he had said, "I have no son to keep my name in memory." He named the pillar after his own name, and to this day it is called the Monument of Absalom.
verses.18:19: And Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, "Let me run, please, and bring news to the king that the LORD has vindicated him from the hand of his enemies."
verses.18:20: Joab said to him, "You are not a bearer of news this day. You may bring news on another day, but on this day you must not bring news, because the king's son is dead."
verses.18:21: Then Joab said to the Cushite, "Go, report to the king what you saw." So the Cushite bowed down to Joab and ran.
